newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AMP Investments NZ still likes NZ equities.
newsitem.headline: AMP Investments NZ still likes NZ equities.

text.p: AMP Investments Ltd said on Tuesday it was overweight in New Zealand equities and planned to stay that way despite poor returns in the March quarter.
Over the March quarter AMP had been overweight in New Zealand shares, holding 26 percent of its NZ$5.6 billion funds under management in shares against its benchmark level of 20 percent.

"We've taken that position in the last quarter so that gives you some idea of the confidence we have in the market," AMP Investments Director Murray Gribben told a news briefing on the fund's quarterly performance.
Paul Dyer, Head of Investment Strategy, said it essentially came down to a valuation argument.

"When we compare the performance of New Zealand shares with their global counterparts, we find New Zealand has somewhat underperformed over the past six months or so. We find New Zealand looking a little bit cheap relative to international shares," Dyer said.
New Zealand equities returned to AMP a negative 3.8 percent over the quarter, but a positive 12.1 percent for the March year.
Dyer said New Zealand bonds were now fairly priced relative to global rates and that drag on equities was now gone.
He said the generally disappointing profit performance during the last quarter had seen many stocks re-rated.
"It is not certain by any means that that process is completely over, but we are a good part into the process and the risk for further downgrades from here is less than it has been."
Dyer said the gross yield for New Zealand equities was very respectable with the year ahead outlook for returns of over seven percent on a par with bonds.
"Given all those things, we don't think there is a tremendous amount of downside to the market."
AMP sees a neutral outlook for New Zealand bonds. It has 27 percent of funds in bonds against the benchmark of 30 percent.
Investment in cash was at historically low levels.
The New Zealand economic framework had been left untouched despite the formation of the new coalition government in December, Gribben said.
He thought the Reserve Bank would be delighted with the March quarter inflation result but the bank would be cautious in the year ahead.
"I believe they will be fairly cautious going into the rest of the year given that we are expecting economic growth to pick up at the end of 1997 and into 1998."
The biggest risk to markets was likely to be further hikes in U.S. official interest rates.
"We believe that in the next few months they will increase short-term interest rates again and inevitably that will have an impact on New Zealand markets," Gribben said.
The property market outlook over the next few years was seen as solid, particularly in the office sector where vacancies were were quite low, said Steve Swain, Head of Property.

Office rentals were rising. The retail property sector outlook looked reasonable despite retail sales falling in the last two quarters while the industrial sector is seen as moving at a reasonable pace.
AMP has around 12 percent of its investment in property against a benchmark of 10 percent.
In the March quarter, AMP Investments' low risk fund returned 0.5 percent, the medium risk fund was negative 0.2 percent and the high risk fund negative 0.6 percent.
March year returns were 9.7 percent for the low and medium risk funds and 10.3 percent for the high risk.
